name: 3469-promptlogprobs-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1, bounded at 200 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup the first 20% by completion; `max-num-seqs: 256` is the ceiling on streams.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn: prompt_tokens fixed at 1000 (min = max), output_tokens fixed at 8 (min = max), seeded 3469, with `prompt_logprobs: 5` and `logprobs: 5` at `temperature: 1.0` / `top_p: 1.0`. `prompt_logprobs: N` asks for the top-N ranking at each PROMPT position, `logprobs: N` at each GENERATED one; 5 is both the OpenAI default and `max-logprobs`, this engine's per-request ceiling. The backend forces `ignore_eos=True` with `max_tokens=8`, so every request generates exactly eight tokens.
purpose: A token-scoring service returning top-5 probabilities over 1000-word prompts and 8-token replies, one user at a time on a single GPU.
launch:
# ERA HAZARD: every key here becomes an `AsyncEngineArgs(**kwargs)` keyword and this engine's
# EngineArgs has 40 fields -- an unknown key is a TypeError at construction, not a warning.
# Do not add keys from a later vLLM (no enable_chunked_prefill, speculative_*,
# num_scheduler_steps, compilation_config, nothing V1). `scheduler-delay-factor` is legal here
# and was removed from vLLM long after this commit: check it in the run venv, not a modern one.

model: NousResearch/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The checkpoint's own `torch_dtype`, pinned so `auto` cannot drift it.
dtype: float16
max-model-len: 4096

# The engine refuses a request asking for more log probabilities per position than this, on
# either the prompt or the output side, so the declared workload sits exactly at the cap.
max-logprobs: 5

max-num-seqs: 256
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
block-size: 16
swap-space: 4
seed: 0
scheduler-delay-factor: 0.0
